chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā, from his father, from Ḥumayd ibn al-Muthannā, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The first bier introduced in Islam was the bier of Fāṭimah عليها السلام.
She suffered the illness in which she was taken, and she said to Asmāʾ: “I have become thin and my flesh has gone; will you not make for me something that covers me?”
Asmāʾ said: “I was in the land of al-Ḥabashah and I saw them making something; shall I not make it for you? If it pleases you, I will make it for you.”

She said: “Yes.” So she called for a bed and turned it face down, then she called for palm stalks and fastened them to its legs, then she covered it with a cloth, and said: “This is how I saw them making it.”
So she said: “Make for me one like it; cover me—may Allah cover you from the Fire.”

key_terms.أَرْضِ الْحَبَشَةِ: the land of Abyssinia, where Asmāʾ had seen this practice
key_terms.جَرَائِدَ: palm stalks or stripped branches used in constructing the bier
key_terms.فَاطِمَةَ عَلَيْهَا السَّلَامُ: Lady Fāṭimah, daughter of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.نَعْشٍ: bier or funeral carriage prepared for the deceased
key_terms.يَسْتُرُنِي: conceals me or covers my body

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the first bier used in Islam for Fāṭimah عليها السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that the first bier of this kind used in Islam was that of Fāṭimah عليها السلام, made to better conceal the form of the deceased. It highlights her modesty even at death and records Asmāʾ’s role in preparing a covered bier based on what she had seen in al-Ḥabashah.
